data.claim: Yes on main 028b910: api.setup.configure(local=True, append_toml=[[reviewer]] kind='command' command=printf 'STATUS: NO FINDINGS' model='gemini-2.5-pro' family='google') is accepted with no operator gate; ddflow review then records critic=passed (reviewer indep, family google), which reviewer_independence counts as cross-family. No existing decision settles who may write reviewer entries: D-no-own-services-local-dir only says WHERE they live, and 4dd7b3e (operator, 2026-10-01) made ddflow_configure's description point agents AT the [[reviewer]] form, so refusing it would reverse a fresh operator choice. Options: (A) configure/_append_config/_write_config refuse [[reviewer]] and reviewer.* over every agent surface, as they refuse gate.<id>.human ('set it in a file no tool writes'); reviewers detect --write keeps writing http entries for servers it actually probed, never kind=command; operator hand-writes command reviewers. (B) provenance: every tool write of a reviewer entry emits a reviewer.configured event (agent, digest of the entry); ddflow review stamps the entry digest into evidence; reviewer_independence refuses evidence from an entry an AGENT wrote until the operator runs a human-only 'ddflow reviewers approve <name>' (mirrors ddflow approve / human:true). (C) both: A for kind=command (arbitrary code, trivially fakeable), B for http entries. Recommendation: C. Neither stops an agent with a shell editing .ddflow/local/*.toml by hand (same limit as human gates: make forgery visible, not impossible); B is what makes it visible.

data.question: Can an agent fabricate an independent review through ddflow_configure (B3f9b8a4ac0), and which remedy fits?

data.body: Bug B3f9b8a4ac0, research Re2a7e01d8e (CONFIRMED). NOT READY TO IMPLEMENT until the operator picks an option: 4dd7b3e (2026-10-01) made ddflow_configure point agents at the [[reviewer]] form, so refusing it reverses a fresh operator choice. (A) configure refuses [[reviewer]]/reviewer.* edits on every agent surface (like gate.<id>.human); reviewers detect --write keeps writing http entries for probed servers only, never kind=command. (B) provenance: a tool-written reviewer entry emits reviewer.configured (agent, entry digest); ddflow review stamps the digest into evidence; reviewer_independence does not count evidence from an agent-written entry until a human-only 'ddflow reviewers approve <name>'. (C, recommended) A for kind=command, B for http. Neither prevents a shell edit of .ddflow/local/*.toml; the aim is visibility, as with human gates.
data.title: PROPOSAL (needs operator decision): an agent cannot mint an independent reviewer — configure refuses kind=command [[reviewer]] entries, and agent-written reviewer entries need operator approval before their reviews count (bug B3f9b8a4ac0)

data.reason: needs operator decision: option A, B or C in the body (research Re2a7e01d8e)

data.body: Bug B7506c1124a. config._coerce_dict returns {str(k): str(v)} for a JSON object given to a dict[str, str] knob, so DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILIES='{"core": null}' loads as {'core': 'None'} and a reviewer named 'core' is classified family 'none'; _coerce's list branch does the same ([null] -> ['None'], [1] -> ['1']). Fix: a JSON value that is not a string is refused with a ValueError naming the key and the JSON type, as the dict[str, list[str]] branch already does. Regression tests in tests/test_env_json_values.py (through Config.load with an env dict, and _coerce directly).
data.title: A string-valued map or list knob set from the environment as JSON refuses a non-string value instead of str()-casting it (null -> 'None') (fixes bug B7506c1124a)

data.body: B289bf87e8d: Reviewer.max_concurrency=4 < chunks x hedge for any diff over 2 chunks, so a review runs in waves (measured 1301-1465 s at 4 vs 1122 s at 12 on 5 chunks x hedge 2). Fix: default 0 = auto, every chunk's copies in one wave (chunks x hedge), bounded by a generic ceiling; a positive value is an explicit cap for a server with few slots. B568e9def3b / B769704d1dc: a reasoning-model reviewer spends max_tokens reasoning and returns no verdict. Lesson Lf3feebf5d3 measured the root cause: at ddflow's default temperature 0.3 DeepSeek loops ('let me reconsider') to the budget on every reasoning_effort; at 1.0 the same diff reviewed fully. The operator's other projects' reviewer entries carry no temperature, so they run at 0.3. Fix (generic, no local values): temperature defaults to unset and is then OMITTED from the request, so the server applies the model's own recommended sampling (vLLM: generation_config; APIs: their default); an explicit value is still sent. The TRUNCATED message names temperature first. A chunk whose every copy came back TRUNCATED is retried once, split in halves when it splits (else whole), within total_budget_s; chunks_total and reporting are unchanged. Tests: tests/test_reviewer_defaults.py.
data.title: Reviewer defaults fit reasoning models: temperature unset by default (the server's/vendor's own), max_concurrency 0 = one wave of chunks x hedge, a chunk whose every copy truncated is retried once in halves, and TRUNCATED names the temperature remedy (fixes bugs B289bf87e8d, B568e9def3b, B769704d1dc)

data.claim: (1) Reviewer.max_concurrency defaults to 4 and _race caps the pool at it, so chunks x hedge > 4 runs in waves. (2) Reviewer.temperature defaults to 0.3 and is always sent; lesson Lf3feebf5d3 measured DeepSeek at 0.3 looping to 64000 reasoning tokens on every reasoning_effort while 1.0 reviewed the same diff fully; the operator's home-simulator and run_nemo_run reviewer entries carry no temperature, so they run at 0.3 (ddflow's own local entry sets 1.0). (3) A chunk whose every copy truncates is reported lost with no second draw, though thinking length is random per call (Rfa535c6747: one call in four never answers on a hard diff).

data.summary: A cancelled hedged copy can crash the whole review: _Cancel shuts the losing copy's socket, and when that copy is mid-read of its response, resp.read() raises http.client.IncompleteRead (an HTTPException, not OSError). _chat_openai and _post_json catch HTTPError/URLError/OSError/ValueError only, so it escapes _chat, _race's fut.result() re-raises it, and review() -- documented 'never raises' -- raises. Seen as a ~1-in-3 flake of a two-copy instant-answer test (tests/test_reviewer_defaults.py) on 29adead; pre-existing on main.

data.title: Reviewer defaults fit reasoning models: temperature unset by default (the model's own), max_concurrency 0 = one wave of chunks x hedge, a chunk whose every copy truncated is retried once in halves, TRUNCATED names the temperature remedy; a hedged copy cut off mid-read no longer crashes the review (fixes bugs B289bf87e8d, B568e9def3b, B769704d1dc, Bf948d29d37)

Noted, not mine: split_diff yields a header-only piece and glues '@@' onto '+++' (B779270c994, being fixed in B-fix-review-chunks); the retry inherits it, harmless (the extra part reviews nothing).

one temperature helper (_temperature) used by all three HTTP backends; _cut_off shared by _post_json and _chat_openai; retry reuses split_diff/_race/parse rather than a second scheduler; _file_headers is new (no existing helper lists diff --git lines)
